newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI STAR NORDIC BOURSE, BUT STILL SMALLEST.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI STAR NORDIC BOURSE, BUT STILL SMALLEST.

text.p: The Helsinki Stock Exchange has advanced more than any Nordic bourse this year and especially in the last 12 months, the Nordic stock exchanges' monthly report showed on Friday.
But Helsinki still has the lowest turnover -- excluding tiny Reykjavik -- at 16.9 billion Ecus for the year to end-July, well behind second thinnest Oslo's 22.3 billion.
Stockholm has been liveliest with 86.0 billion Ecu turnover and Copenhagen second with 24.6 billion Ecus.
Helsinki stocks had advanced 44.9 percent by the end of July with second-best Copenhagen at 36.9 percent and Oslo and Stockholm at 33.1 percent.
In the 12 months to end-July, the Helsinki main index has added 83.4 percent, with Stockholm at 68.0 percent, Oslo at 59.5 percent and Copenhagen at 59.1 percent.

Still, Helsinki's strong gains -- up 12.7 percent in July -- are modest compared to the emerging bourse in southern neighbour Estonia, where the main index has risen around 50 percent since the start of July.

By domestic equity market capitalisation, Stockholm is clearly the largest Nordic bourse: at 256.3 billion Ecus it is bigger than the sum of Copenhagen's 80.7 billion, Helsinki's 73.1 billion, Oslo's 59.9 billion and Reykjavik's 2.0 billion.
